judges: Where There Is No Chance Of Reconciliation J.
trial_court: Family Court, Gurugram, CR No. 3071 of 2019
case_name: Dharamveer vs Rekha Maurya @ Rekha Rani
facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2014 and had a child. They decided to take divorce by mutual consent. A petition under Section 13-B of Hindu Marriage Act was filed on 01.04.2019.

legal_principles.principle: The statutory period under Section 13-B (2) of the Hindu Marriage Act is directory and not mandatory.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that the period mentioned in Section 13-B (2) of Hindu Marriage Act is not mandatory, rather the same is directory and it is open to the Court to exercise its discretion in the facts and circumstances of the case.

legal_principles.principle: The court has to consider the interest of justice and the possibility of resuming cohabitation between the parties before exercising its discretion.
legal_principles.held: The Court has to see whether there is any possibility of resuming cohabitation between the parties or there is any chance of rehabilitation.

legal_principles.principle: The court has to consider the period for which the parties have been married before exercising its discretion.
legal_principles.held: The Court has to consider the period for which the parties have been married.

legal_principles.principle: The court has to consider the interest of the minor child before exercising its discretion.
legal_principles.held: Adequate arrangement has been made for the minor child towards her past, present and future maintenance.

outcome.final_order: Statutory cooling period of six months was not dispensed with.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce by mutual consent
advising on the cooling period in Hindu Marriage Act cases
understanding the role of family courts in India
